title: Compact Onramp Lab Journal: rapid 10-min SDK paths
content:
Purpose:
A compact experimental journal for designing a 10-minute, low-friction SDK onramp. This is intentionally messy — a sequence of micro-experiments, quick scripts, sample prompts, and shortnotes from pairing sessions. Goal is to end up with: (a) a one-page quickstart that really gets a user to a first successful call in <10 minutes, and (b) 3 tiny code samples (curl, python, node) that are copy-paste safe.

Background & constraints:
- Users: engineers who want to wire a Redwood text/generation call into a demo or product prototype quickly.
- Constraints: minimal install, minimal account setup friction, no infra knowledge required. Use hosted API defaults, show how to swap in Dedicated later.
- Design principles: 1) pragmatic over perfect; 2) explicitly show failure/retry; 3) show telemetry/backoff hints.

Experiment notes (chronological):
2024-12-06 — baseline quickstart prototype\- First-run: curl + python snippets. Problem: python snippet used requests.Session but forgot to show how to export REDWOOD_API_KEY; many users hit auth errors.\- Fix: add explicit auth export step and a sanity-check curl that returns 200 with explanatory message.

2024-12-12 — 5-minute wiring test with new hires (2 participants)\- Observed: participants skimmed long paragraphs; they copy-pasted but didn't run due to missing newline in the multi-line prompt example.\- Action: convert multi-line prompts to single-line escaped JSON examples or triple-quoted block marked as optional.

2024-12-18 — network-sim test (lossy mobile)\- Added small note on client-side timeout and exponential backoff (example: 500ms initial, *2, max 4s)\- Try to keep streaming examples optional (advanced).

2025-01-07 — pairing with Console team\- Added link to Console route for viewing requests, and a quick note: "If your request appears but no tokens returned, check model fallback in Console -> Models."

Draft one-page quickstart (intended to be copy-paste friendly):
1) Get an API key
   - Sign up at https://app.redwood.ai and create API key "demo-key" (or use existing).

2) Environment (Linux/Mac):
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=demo-key

3) Sanity check (curl):
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-small-1","input":"Hello from my terminal! Return a single short sentence."}'

   Expected: JSON containing "output" with a short sentence. If 401 -> check env var and key. If 429 -> reduce concurrency or try again.

4) Minimal Python (copy/paste):
   python sample:
   """
   # file: quick_example.py
   import os
   import requests
   KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
   assert KEY, 'export REDWOOD_API_KEY before running'
   resp = requests.post(
       'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
       headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
       json={'model': 'redwood-small-1', 'input': 'Write a two-sentence description of Redwood Inference.'}
   )
   print(resp.json())
   """

5) Quick Node snippet (copy/paste):
   node sample:
   """
   // file: quick_example.js
   // requires: node >= 16
   const fetch = require('node-fetch')
   if (!process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) throw new Error('export REDWOOD_API_KEY')
   fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
     method: 'POST',
     headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
     body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small-1', input: 'Summarize in one line why inference matters.' })
   }).then(r => r.json()).then(console.log).catch(console.error)
   """

Failure modes to call out (short):
- Auth (401): missing key or wrong environment. Add quick command to show env: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | sed -n '1p'`
- Rate limit (429): show HTTP Retry-After header and recommend backoff.
- Bad model name (400): surface available models command (TODO: add `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models`).

Micro-experiments to run next week:
- A/B: single-page vs two-column quickstart (left: steps, right: copy-paste code). Which leads to faster first-success? Measure in user test.
- Add a tiny 'first-success' telemetry ping from sample app (opt-in) to Console so we can measure drop-off at step boundaries. Privacy notes required.
- Create a tiny GitHub template repo with a single file demo and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the curl check.

Prompt hygiene and sample prompts (rules-of-thumb):
- Keep an example prompt short and deterministic.
- Show a multi-turn stub but mark as advanced.
- Avoid dataset/PII examples. Use synthetic examples like "a two-sentence product blurb".

Safety/Privacy note (short):
- Quickstarts must not encourage copying real user data into public demos. Add a small red callout: "Do not paste private user PII into shared public examples."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where does the canonical quickstart live? Confluence? Docs site? (link proposals in linked_artifacts)
- Should we include a streaming example in the first page or leave it for "advanced"? My leaning: leave streaming for advanced; show a clear path to it.
- Add a 1-click Try in Console button (engineering help needed from Console team).
- Internationalization: add notes for non-English locales and sample text variations.

Observations from test participants (one-liners):
- "I want a button that runs the curl and tells me success/failure." — Frontend eng
- "Show me the minimal code that will paste into my existing node express app." — Backend eng
- "The sample Python printed a giant dict; make it print only output text." — Data scientist

Quick checklist for final quickstart (MVP):
- [ ] One-page quickstart with 3 copy-paste examples (curl, python, node).
- [ ] Explicit auth sanity check and troubleshooting bullet.
- [ ] Tiny error/429/backoff guidance.
- [ ] Link to Console request inspector.
- [ ] GitHub template repo + tiny workflow for CI smoke checks.
- [ ] Short privacy callout.
- [ ] Measurement: add telemetry opt-in in sample to track first-success (spec + telemetry ticket).

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep language minimal; skip long paragraphs. Use numbered steps and code boxes.
- Avoid advanced features on first page; keep streaming/fn-calling/embeddings as follow-ups.

Session logs (quick, raw):
- 2025-01-10 pairing with Lena: refactor python sample to print `resp.json().get('output', '')` instead of printing whole body.\- 2025-01-15 Omar validated curl on Windows WSL and noted that `sed` hints break on Windows; add a Windows note: `powershell -Command "$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY"`

Appendix: user-friendly failure messages (copyable)
- auth: `if resp.status_code == 401: raise Exception('401: check REDWOOD_API_KEY, run: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY')`
- rate-limit: `if resp.status_code == 429: print(resp.headers.get('Retry-After'))`

End of journal entry.

(If you want to run a quick usability test, ping me — Maya — and I will schedule 3 back-to-back 10-min sessions; we'll record success time and UX friction points.)
